result_paragraph: Gate Q16 is **not passing** and `passes` is set nowhere. By decision DD-PM-01 there are still **0 documented camera positions** (a coordinate, a lens and a plate): none of the 161 position statements (Library of Congress records, National Park Service reports, place pages and the Record of Treatment) is one. What is new: (1) the National Park Service names the camera place of two catalogued exposures as a building of known outline, the first documented camera places: the roof of the Evergreen Cemetery lodge (view north: records 2018671576 and 2014646001, poses P27 north and P28 northwest, two words of two NPS texts for one exposure) and the gatehouse (view east: record 2012647704, pose P29); their height, lens and exact heading are not documented. (2) The pass criteria of the tests at those places were written before the renders (criteria.json). Results: P27 roughly, P28 does not, P29 roughly; P13 (rendered now) roughly. The three binary tests of the first criterion are necessary conditions only (the superseded poses P06 and P07 pass them too and are does not); the skyline tests fit the heading, the lens and a vertical shift to the photograph and are compared with 24 control stations: P27 (north sector): RMS 0.0938 degrees (match-level) at heading -0.5, field 25; rank 14 of 25 against 24 controls (quartile 0.0934, median 0.0937); discriminated False; P28 (northwest sector): RMS 0.1043 degrees (match-level) at heading -24.5, field 25; rank 14 of 25 against 24 controls (quartile 0.1041, median 0.1043); discriminated False; P29 (east sector): RMS 0.5608 degrees (partial) at heading 93.25, field 25; rank 19 of 25 against 24 controls (quartile 0.4379, median 0.5393); discriminated False. No pose is called a match. (3) The Record of Treatment prints 36 captioned 1863 photographs with a direction of view; 24 are tied to catalogued Library of Congress records (22 by image match confirmed by looking, 20 of them with same-plate geometry; the others by the Digital ID in the caption), the others are prints of the park and other collections. The image ties of the six Metropolitan Museum items show that the first run's P04 and P05 are the two plates of one Library panorama (record 2014646002). (4) A wider search of the Library of Congress (the whole Civil War group) added 62 records (37 tied to a catalogued exposure by looking; 6 high-scoring matches were rejected on looking): the registry now holds 191 records and 20 poses. (5) Re-running the renderer reproduced the renders of the earlier sessions pixel for pixel (see the determinism line below). (6) The fourth session (2026-11-15) finished what the restarts of 2026-11-14 had cut short: P29 rendered and its sheet looked at, the verdicts of P13, P27, P28 and P29 written (the P29 verdict is weak: the skyline test does not tell the gatehouse from its neighbours), a full re-run of all 20 poses reproduced every render byte for byte, an error in the drafted P29 text found and fixed (18 of the 24 control stations fit better than the gatehouse, not 6), and the registry texts that said no place or direction was stated where the Park Service gives one corrected. What would settle Q16: station coordinates, lens and plate from the park (an owner step), the height and 1863 form of the gatehouse, a 1863 near-field model, landmark coordinates good to a few metres, and a value for T-Q16-1 written before the match (all in PHOTOMATCH.md).

findings: The National Park Service's Record of Treatment (2018) is a source of camera directions and, for some, camera places for about forty July 1863 photographs (park numbers 2B-2063, 2B-2090 and so on); the park's own catalogue is the next step toward stations (owner step). The captions double as 1863 landscape evidence (orchards, fences, woodlots of the Rose, Sherfy, Weikert and McPherson farms): the nps-landscape and vegetation lanes may cite them.
The model's outline of the Evergreen Cemetery gatehouse is the 2023 footprint with the right-hand addition; the camera stood on or in the 1855 building (EG-13).
Two NPS texts give two words for the direction of the lodge-roof view, north and northwest; read from the photograph (an exploratory reading, not a test) the heading lies at their boundary (EG-14).

The Leister house photograph (cwpb 00887) is called a view north along the Taneytown Road by the Then-And-Now page and a view northwest by the Record of Treatment: a 45-degree conflict carried as statements; pose P18 follows the first.

The old test tests/photomatch.test.mjs fails on the new ledger and schema (request note bt-web-photomatch-old-test.md); the Q16 section of GATE-SPEC should be refreshed from the files (request note bt-gates-photomatch-third-pass.md).

A feature-match score is not an identification: six matches of 109 to 286 inliers were false (studio portraits and a card with a flag matched to landscapes, a road view matched to a stereo card), and the rule class of tie_geometry.py disagreed with the eye for two true ties (reported as the rule gave them). Every tie was therefore looked at, and the stereo cards were called by looking at their halves.

The first run's poses P04 and P05 (Metropolitan Museum prints) are the two plates of the Library panorama 2014646002 (View of Gettysburg from the Northwest); the Seminary Ridge standpoint of both is still an assumption and the verdict (does not) is on that assumed pose.

The Record of Treatment and the other National Park Service texts disagree on the direction of two Library photographs without a place: park print 2B-2083a (record 2018672207, Little Round Top slope) is a view southeast in the Record of Treatment, against southwest near Devil's Den and northwest at Wheatfield Road and Crawford Avenue in the vista report; park print 2B2086 (record 2018670709) is a view south there. Carried as statements, none chosen.

The camera place of the Library record 2018670660 (five images of one exposure) is the Rose Barn according to the Record of Treatment (view southwest), but the frame holds only a grave trench, grave boards, a tree and a wagon train: a near-field view that the bare-earth model cannot be compared with; the barn is a point of the model (error 10 m), not a footprint.

A fitted skyline cannot decide a station: for P29 the three best-fitting of 24 control stations lie 200 to 300 m east or south-east on ground 17 to 19 m lower, and the fit is as good at 5 m, 8 m and 11 m camera height (0.53 to 0.58 degrees).

The verso of the Tyson card 2019635468 ([Gettysburg from Seminary Ridge]) carries, besides the studio stamp and the ink word Gettysburg (all the Library transcribes), a faint pencil note in another hand: 'original by Tyson in August 1863' (read at 1024 px; hand and date of the note unknown). If it is right the view is of August, not of July 1863; the record stays inside the July terrain scope as a lead, flagged in its registry entry.

The second resource of record 2014647511 (John Burns, the hero of Gettysburg / Slaughter pen at Gettysburg) is the verso of the card, a second picture: a small print of the slaughter pen with the card's caption No. 253. The registry had said the verso was not shown; it now says what it shows (a near-field wood view).

fifth.result_paragraph: Gate Q16 is **not passing** and `passes` is set nowhere. There are still **0 documented camera positions** (a coordinate, a lens and a plate: decision DD-PM-01); none of the 161 camera-position statements now read gives one. What this session found: (1) **no photograph remained unread**: every digitized record of the registry had been fetched and looked at in the earlier sessions (the ledgers list 447 files of the first catalogue, 57 of the wide search and 82 further resources, each with sha256 and size; every entry has its saved file on disk, 11 originals of the first run having been deleted by design with their working copies kept, and the test file re-checks sizes and hashes wherever the file is present); the only records without an image are the 5 that the Library has not digitized. (2) **All 191 Library records were read again** from the open JSON of each record (191 fetched, 0 failed, 0 changed since the first reading); 37 hold a sentence that names a place or direction of view; each is a statement or has a written reading of why it is not (the place of the subject, a later photograph, a portrait); 4 records got a statement they had lacked (the Emmitsburg Road caption of 2018670908, the Rose-woods wording of 2008680497 and 2018670757 as leads, the staged card 2004682792 as a lead). (3) **A new primary source**: the Library holds Gardner's Photographic Sketch Book of the War as images only, but the master scans of the letterpress pages of the ten Gettysburg plates (35 to 44) are legible to OCR; they were read by machine and by eye. Plate 35, 'Gettysburg, Pennsylvania' (the exposure of poses P27 and P28), says in Gardner's own words: 'This view is taken from Cemetery Ridge, where our artillery was massed' and 'on the left of the picture can be seen Seminary Ridge'. It is a second source for the place, it names a ridge and not a building, and it gives no spot, bearing, height or lens; nine of the ten pages say nothing about where the camera stood. Gardner's catalogue of September 1863 (Library copy, OCR) and the Library's essays 'Does the Camera Ever Lie?' were read too: 16 statements were added in all (now 161; 13 from the new sources and records; 2 from the National Park Service cemetery report, read again for the form of the gate lodge: a two-story archway with two floors of lodge quarters in the flanking piers, and a two-story frame addition on the rear built after the battle; and 1 from the Library's physical description of the lodge-roof negative: a glass stereograph plate of 4 x 10 in., which corrects the earlier statements that no source gives a plate size: the plate is documented for 16 negatives, the lens and the coordinate for none); the essays say their analysis rests on Frassanito, so their statements of place are leads. (4) The staged-photograph flag of the sharpshooter series, which rested on the plan and on an unread National Archives blog, now also carries readable official words (NPS Then-And-Now: 'nor is it likely that the soldier fell in this location'; the body 'moved by the photographers from this location to another one some 40 yards away'; the Library essay: the photographers 'moved the corpse to this rocky niche and photographed him again'). (5) **The National Park Service texts were scanned again** with the same rule: 325 texts (the 118 of the earlier passes and 207 saved since, among them 51 HABS data pages, park newsletters and 12 hub pages fetched today), 359 passages, 19 in the new texts, none about the camera place of a July 1863 photograph. (6) **The renderer was re-run** for all 20 poses through the machine lock (120 files in 33 s): every file is byte-identical to the one the earlier sessions looked at, a second independent reproduction; compose.py rebuilt the 25 sheets, byte-identical to the earlier ones. (7) **All 20 pose sheets and the five lines images were opened and looked at again**; every verdict was read against its sheet; none changed: 0 matches, 8 roughly, 5 does not, 7 cannot judge over 20 poses (P27 roughly, P28 does not, P29 roughly, P13 roughly). No pose is called a match, and none can be: a fitted test is not a match and T-Q16-1 is unset. **What would settle Q16** (unchanged, and now narrower): station coordinates, lens and plate from the body that has them (the Gettysburg National Military Park: its museum or GIS staff for the Historic Photograph Collection prints GETT 41135 and the Then-And-Now stations; an owner act), the height and the 1863 form of the Evergreen Cemetery gatehouse, an 1863 near-field model, landmark coordinates good to a few metres, and a value for T-Q16-1 written before the match.

findings: The NPS Cultural Landscape Report for Gettysburg National Cemetery, read again for the height and form of the gate lodge, says that the Evergreen lodge (begun 1 September 1855) is an Italianate two-story archway with two floors of lodge quarters in the flanking piers, and (page 73 of the saved text) that after the battle the Evergreen Cemetery Association repaired the gatehouse, including a two-story frame addition on the rear. So the one-storey default of the model is wrong for the building, the assumed 8 m camera height is consistent with two storeys and a roof but not documented, and the 2023 outline that the model holds, which includes an addition, may not be the form of July 1863 (EG-13). No height in metres is given.

The Library's physical description gives the plate of 16 negatives (glass, stereograph, wet collodion, 4 x 10 in.), among them the lodge-roof exposure (2018671576), and the plate type of most others; the earlier reports said that no source gives a plate size. The plate is therefore documented for those negatives; no record gives a lens, so the field of view stays an assumption, and no source gives a coordinate: the count of documented camera positions (all three) stays 0.

Gardner's letterpress for plate 35 gives three readings for the heading of the Evergreen Cemetery lodge exposure that no single heading meets at an assumed 40 degree field: north (the Cemetery Landscape Report), northwest (the Record of Treatment) and Seminary Ridge on the left of the picture (Gardner). At the north word the Seminary and the ridge lie outside the frame; at the northwest word the ridge stands at 0.18 and the Seminary at 0.47 of the frame width but the pike falls at the right edge and the court house is outside the frame; the tower-implied heading (337 to 343 degrees, a fit and not a test) lies between. All three are carried, none chosen (EG-14, DD-PM-15).

The Sketch Book (1866) credits plate 35 to T. H. O'Sullivan; Gardner's catalogue of September 1863 lists no. 273 'Gettysburg from the Cemetery' (the negative number the NPS cites, LC-B815-273) in a block of negatives that the ditto marks of its OCR text assign to Jas. F. Gibson. Attribution does not bear on the camera place and is carried, not resolved.
